name: Sweet potatoes
summary: Sweet potatoes are a starchy root vegetable with orange, white or purple flesh. This page lists what people say sweet potatoes do; each claim can be checked against the research when you choose. Sweet potatoes came from the Americas, so ancient Greek and Roman writers did not know them and there is no Then and now.
inIt: Orange-fleshed sweet potatoes are rich in carotenoids, the plant pigments the body can turn into vitamin A, and a 2019 review describes them as used against vitamin A deficiency in parts of Africa. Purple ones hold anthocyanins.

How it is cooked changes the glycaemic index (how fast a food raises blood sugar): in a test of ten varieties in 10 healthy adults, values ranged from 41 to 93, and boiling gave the lowest (41 to 50).

The UK food table (CoFID) measures baked sweet potato at 115 kcal, 27.9 g of carbohydrate (14.5 g of sugars), 5.2 g of fibre, 480 mg of potassium, 855 µg of vitamin A (as retinol equivalents) and 23 mg of vitamin C per 100 g. It does not measure anthocyanins or the separate carotenoids.

processing: Cooking method changes the glycaemic index: boiling gave the lowest values (41 to 50) in the ten-variety test.
The 2022 review says the effect of cooking on sweet potato's plant compounds needs more study to know how to limit their loss.
In the UK food table, raw sweet potato holds 5.7 g of sugars per 100 g and baked holds 14.5 g.

whoShouldBeCareful.note: The glycaemic index of sweet potato ranged from 41 to 93 in one study depending on variety and cooking, so one sweet potato dish does not predict another. If you manage diabetes, talk to your doctor or dietitian about how it fits your meals.

unknowns: Whether eating sweet potatoes changes health outcomes in people: the reviews describe lab, animal and small human findings, and this page does not rate them.
How much carotenoid a given sweet potato has: it varies by variety, colour and how it is cooked.
Whether purple varieties do anything more than orange or white ones in people.
